1.text:
(Pro. 20:1-30)

mocker--scorner. Such men are made by wine.

strong drink--made by spicing wine (compare Isa 5:11, Isa 5:22); and it may include wine.

raging--or boisterous as a drunkard.

deceived--literally, "erring," or reeling.

2.text: (Compare Pro 19:12). Men who resist authority injure themselves (Rom 13:2).

3.text:
to cease from strife--or, better, "to dwell from or without strife," denoting the habit of life.

fool . . . meddling-- (Pro 17:14).

5.text: Counsel . . . water--that is, deeply hidden (Pro 18:4; Psa 13:2). The wise can discern well.

7.text: The conduct of good men proclaims their sound principles. God's covenant and their good example secure blessing to their children (Pro 4:26; Psa 112:1-2).

8.text: As in Pro 14:35; Pro 16:10, Pro 16:15, this is the character of a good king, not of all kings.

9.text: The interrogation in the affirmative strengthens the implied negation (compare Job 15:14; Ecc 7:20).

10.text: Various measures, implying that some are wrong (compare Pro 11:1; Pro 16:11).

11.text: The conduct of children even is the best test of principle (compare Mat 7:16).

12.text: Hence, of course, God will know all you do (Psa 94:9).

13.text:
Activity and diligence contrasted with sloth (Pro 6:9; Pro 10:11).

lest . . . poverty--literally, "be deprived of inheritance."

14.text: when . . . his way--implying that he goes about boasting of his bargains.

15.text: The contrast denotes the greater value of knowledge (compare Pro 3:14-16).

16.text:
Take his garment--implies severe exaction, justified by the surety's rashness.

a strange woman--by some readings "strangers," but the former here, and in Pro 27:13, is allowable, and strengthens the sense. The debauchee is less reliable than the merely careless.

17.text:
Bread . . . sweet--either as unlawfully (Pro 9:17) or easily obtained.

mouth . . . gravel--well expresses the pain and grief given at last.

18.text: (Compare Pro 15:22). Be careful and considerate in important plans.

19.text:
Those who love to tell news will hardly keep secrets.

flattereth . . . lips--(compare Margin; Pro 1:10).

meddle . . . him--literally, "join," or "associate with."

21.text: gotten hastily--contrary to God's providence (Pro 28:20), implying its unjust or easy attainment; hence the man is punished, or spends freely what he got easily (compare Pro 20:17).

24.text:
Man's goings--literally, "Stately steppings of a strong man."

a man--any common man.

understand--or, "perceive."

25.text: devoureth . . . holy--or, better, "who rashly speaks promises," or "devotes what is holy," consecrating any thing. This suits better the last clause, which expresses a similar view of the results of rashly vowing.

26.text:
(Compare Pro 20:8).

bringeth . . . over them--The wheel was used for threshing grain. The figure denotes severity (compare Amo 1:3).

27.text: The spirit . . . Lord--Men's minds are God's gifts, and thus able to search one another (compare Pro 20:5; Pro 18:8, Pro 18:17; Co1 2:11).

29.text: The glory of young men . . . the beauty of old men--Each age has its peculiar excellence (Pro 16:31).

30.text:
blueness--literally, "joining," the process of uniting the edges of a wound throws off purulent matter.

stripes . . . belly--So punishment provides healing of soul (Pro 18:8), by deterring from evil courses.
